text: just commit all the work its not a problem
resolution: Compiled-game (no-V8) root cause found via RJIT_COLLIDERLOG and fixed. The log showed loaded(oriented=16384) — the MAX_ORIENTED cap — while the bake built only 33 oriented colliders; the other ~16k were DECORATIVE FOLIAGE. The flora recipe (req_1591, a parallel session) expands tens of thousands of grass/bush/frond/flower cells into render instances, and the loader's instance-derived physics paths (emitRowCollider for windowed huge maps + the buildPhysicsColliders fallback) turned EACH render instance into a physics collider with no foliage filter. So the player bumped invisible flowers (taller blade colliders exceed step height), and the blades saturated the oriented budget, crowding real walls/props and the sign's elevated beam box out of the near-field window — producing the phantom walls on stairs and the lost walk-under under the sign/roofs. Fix: new isNonCollidingFoliage(SHAPE_GRASS/BUSH/FROND/FLOWER) skips those rows in BOTH instance-collider paths; palm TRUNKS and all structural shapes still collide; foliage is walk-through (cards + concealment). Loader compiles (zig build -Dapp-source=world_loader.zig -Duse-v8=false -Dhas-gpu=true -Doptimize=ReleaseFast, exit 0). world_loader.zig was committed whole at the user's direction — it also carries the parallel flora-recipe instance expansion and builds clean together. Diagnostic shipped earlier this thread: RJIT_COLLIDERLOG summary (bd3eb6bcd) + per-collider detail dump (668f0c4a5) that named the wrong colliders by band/solid flag. User must rebuild + recompile to pick this up.
